raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
### What does this PR do?

Fixes two ways Megatron QAT breaks because of the layer spec the engine builds the model from, and corrects the Hopper note in the QAT guide. Both came out of the MXFP4 recipe checks reported in #8186.

**1. Models whose Megatron-Bridge bridge sets its own layer spec fail under QAT.** With QAT enabled, the engine replaced every provider's `transformer_layer_spec` with `modelopt_transformer_layer_spec`. Megatron-Bridge maps the HF weights onto the modules of the spec the bridge chose, and more than twenty bridges set their own (OLMoE, Qwen3-Next, text-only Qwen3.5, DeepSeek-V2/V3/V4, GLM, Kimi, MiniMax, ...). Under the ModelOpt spec those models lose modules. OLMoE fails at load:

```
ValueError: Shape mismatch for megatron param decoder.layers.0.self_attention.k_layernorm.weight
```

By the same code path, Qwen3-Next and text-only Qwen3.5 would lose their linear-attention layers (from reading the bridges; not run). Qwen3.5 checkpoints (`Qwen3_5MoeForConditionalGeneration`) only escape because the Qwen3.5 VL provider builds its language block without reading `transformer_layer_spec`, so their QAT already runs on the TE spec.

The engine now switches to the ModelOpt spec only when the provider uses Bridge's default GPT spec (`default_layer_spec`). Any other spec is kept, and ModelOpt quantizes its Transformer Engine modules in place (`TELayerNormColumnParallelLinear`, `TERowParallelLinear`, the grouped expert linears, ...). Models on the default spec are unchanged.

**2. Packed THD sequences fail at the first forward when context parallelism is 1** (`use_remove_padding=True`, the default):

```
AssertionError: Attention mask type must be padding or padding_causal for qkv_format=thd!
```

When `use_arbitrary_attention_mask` is unset, `modelopt_transformer_layer_spec` turns it on for CP=1; the arbitrary mask is meant for speculative-decoding training. Transformer Engine then rejects verl's THD inputs. This PR defaults the flag to `False` under the ModelOpt spec, which keeps the causal mask that the non-QAT TE spec uses. An explicit `override_transformer_config.use_arbitrary_attention_mask` still wins.

**3. Docs.** `docs/low_precision/qat.md`:
- The `MXFP4` preset has no Marlin fallback: its MXFP4-weight × FP8-activation experts are served only by vLLM's DeepGEMM FP4 MoE kernel (SM100/SM120), so on Hopper the rollout fails at engine start.
- New limitation: the ModelOpt spec's expert module (`SequentialMLP`) rejects tensor and expert parallelism together, so default-spec models need TP=1 or EP=1 under QAT. Models with their own spec keep it.

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Search for similar PRs: no open PR or issue mentions `use_arbitrary_attention_mask`, `modelopt_transformer_layer_spec`, the THD assertion, or QAT with a model-specific layer spec (searched `use_arbitrary_attention_mask`, `qat thd`, `modelopt_transformer_layer_spec`, `QAT layer spec`, `qat transformer_layer_spec`, `QAT olmoe`, `QAT custom spec`, and the error text). #7971 changes the same file but not the QAT layer spec.
- [x] Format the PR title as `[{modules}] {type}: {description}`.

### Test

```bash
python -m pytest -q tests/workers/test_megatron_qat_layer_spec_on_cpu.py tests/workers/test_megatron_*_on_cpu.py \
  tests/workers/test_engine_*_on_cpu.py tests/workers/test_router_replay_engine_helpers_on_cpu.py \
  tests/utils/test_mxfp8_ignored_layers_on_cpu.py
# 80 passed
bash scripts/generate_trainer_config.sh
# All good
pre-commit run --files <changed files>
# ruff, ruff format, mypy, docs time, docstring, license and structure checks pass
```

The CPU test covers the default-spec switch, an explicit mask override, and keeping a bridge-specific spec.

Spec chosen by `_use_qat_layer_spec` on real Megatron-Bridge 0.6.2 providers (CPU, built from the HF configs as the engine does, no weights loaded):

| Model | Bridge spec | Spec under QAT |
|---|---|---|
| OLMoE-1B-7B-0125-Instruct | `olmoe_layer_spec` | kept (was replaced) |
| Qwen3-MoE | `default_layer_spec` | `modelopt_transformer_layer_spec` (unchanged) |
| Qwen3.5-35B-A3B | experimental attention variant | kept (the VL provider ignores the field anyway) |
| Qwen3.5 MoE, text-only config | experimental attention variant | kept (was replaced) |

GPU, 1× GH200 with the stock wheelhouse TE, `scripts/rollout_logprob_diff.py --n-gpus 1 --tp 1 --gen-tp 1 --ep 1 --quant-linear FP8_BLOCK --quant-moe FP8_BLOCK`, OLMoE-1B-7B-0125-Instruct:

| Code | QAT | Result | k3 KL |
|---|---|---|---|
| THD fix only (first commit) | `--qat-mode fp8` | fails at load with the `k_layernorm` shape mismatch above | — |
| this PR | `--qat-mode fp8` | runs; 128 enabled quantizers, all on TE modules (layernorm-column, row, grouped fc1 and fc2 linears) | 6.3e-3 |
| this PR | off | runs | 9.1e-3 |

- The rollout starts from dummy weights and receives the trainer's export through `update_weights()`. The QAT run therefore also exercises exporting the quantized TE modules, grouped experts included, through the OLMoE bridge.
- The quantizer count came from a temporary debug print that is not part of this PR.
- OLMoE is the only model with its own spec that I ran on GPU. The other bridge-specific models now keep their own spec by the same code path; I did not run them.

THD part, `scripts/rollout_logprob_diff.py` with Megatron QAT, CP=1, `use_remove_padding=True`, on a small Qwen3-MoE (random init, 4 layers, 32 experts):

- **Before the fix**, on GH200 with the stock wheelhouse TE (`--quant-linear FP8_BLOCK --quant-moe FP8_BLOCK --qat-mode fp8`) and on an RTX 5090 (`--quant-moe MXFP4 --qat-mode mxfp4`): the assertion above fires at the first actor forward.
- **With the equivalent override** `+actor_rollout_ref.actor.megatron.override_transformer_config.use_arbitrary_attention_mask=False`: both run to completion. On the 5090, MXFP4 QAT gives k3 KL 2.3e-4, against 1.7e-3 for the same MXFP4 rollout without QAT.
- These THD runs used the override, not this branch. The code path in this PR sets the same provider field through `provider_overrides`.

Hopper doc claim: on GH200 with vLLM 0.29, loading the trainer-exported MXFP4 preset fails for every backend:
- `auto` raises `NotImplementedError: No MXFP4 MoE backend supports the deployment configuration`;
- `deep_gemm` reports an unsupported device;
- `marlin` and `triton` reject the FP8 1x128 activation scheme;
- `rollout_logprob_diff.py --quant-moe MXFP4` fails at engine start.

### Design & Code Changes

- `verl/workers/engine/megatron/transformer_impl.py`: QAT spec selection moves into `_use_qat_layer_spec(provider, provider_overrides)`. It returns early unless the provider uses `default_layer_spec`; otherwise it sets `modelopt_transformer_layer_spec` and `provider_overrides.setdefault("use_arbitrary_attention_mask", False)`.
- `tests/workers/test_megatron_qat_layer_spec_on_cpu.py`: new CPU test.
- `docs/low_precision/qat.md`: Hopper note for the `MXFP4` preset and the QAT layer-spec limitation.

### Checklist Before Submitting

- [x] Read the [Contribute Guide](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [x] Apply pre-commit checks.
- [x] Add / Update the documentation.
- [x] Add unit tests (CPU).

Thanks @wuxibin89 for merging, and for the simplification in 781c0dc.

For anyone reading the squash message: 781c0dc removed `_use_qat_layer_spec`, its CPU test and the TP=1/EP=1 note before the merge. Megatron QAT now quantizes the Transformer Engine modules of the bridge's own spec in place for every model, including default-spec models such as Qwen3-MoE. The commit message still describes the earlier version, in which default-spec models switched to the ModelOpt spec. Without the ModelOpt spec, packed THD inputs keep the causal mask they use without QAT. The Qwen3.5-35B-A3B reference numbers in `qat.md` were already measured on this path, because the Qwen3.5 VL provider ignores the spec field.

On the TE spec I have run OLMoE with FP8 QAT on GH200 (numbers in the description). I have not run a default-spec MoE on the TE spec, or QAT with TP>1 and EP>1 together. The MXFP4 recipe on #8186 uses Qwen3-30B-A3B, a default-spec MoE, so its results will cover that path.
